events.title: Catrìona's request to Silas Crewe
events.body: Catrìona nic Eachainn, crew-leader of the seventh shift at Baile thais, asks the agent Silas Crewe to close the third and fourth galleries, where the Green Death struck worst, until the surgeon rules on the dust. Crewe answers that the yield must not fall on a physician's guess, and says only that he will write it up.

events.title: Sìneag searches the old rolls for a law of rest
events.body: Asked by Catrìona nic Eachainn whether any old law binds a hill's rest, the custodian Sìneag of Baile thais searches her rolls and finds none: Lagh an Loscaidh Bhig governs the coal burned, not the coal cut, and no custodian before this age had needed to write a law about men sickening below ground.

events.title: Sìneag's rolls note a granary built against a stoppage
events.body: The custodian Sìneag writes in her rolls that she has never before read of a granary raised to answer a stoppage rather than a harvest, and sets the words down as they stand, without further comment, for whoever should read the roll after her.

events.title: Three priests will not stand for the blessing
events.body: Three of the younger priests of Òrd Mhacha stand apart at the back of the temple hall rather than take their places for the blessing of the coin. Beathag Ruadh lets it pass unremarked before the Residency's clerk, and tells Fearghas mac Mhuirich only that the order answers for the rite done rightly, not for the road a rightly blessed thing afterward walks.

events.title: Artair mac Iain seated after ten empty years
events.body: The Council of Custodians, unable to agree a head since Alasdair Liath's death, seats Artair mac Iain of the eastern shires as high custodian, six-and-fifty years old, in the hall where Tormod mac Ailein once signed the treaty. Fearghas mac Mhuirich says the order's blessing over him, both horses named.

events.title: The Residency notes the order divided
events.body: Word of Fearghas mac Mhuirich's refusal reaches the Residency within the month. Tolley, near his own retiring, does not send for him; the Residency's letter-book records only that the order of Òrd Mhacha at the capital is divided on a religious nicety, and does not say what the nicety was.

events.title: The Levy read at Cnoc thais
events.body: The Levy's officers read their list at Cnoc thais, and the mason Dùghall Clachair hears his own name and his whole crew's called for the pits. Two days into the eastward march they are turned out instead to the headland at Baile chrom, where the fifth and last coast beacon is begun.

events.title: A gale strips the beacon's scaffold
events.body: A two-day gale out of the north-west tears the scaffolding from the third course of the rising tower at Baile chrom. Dùghall Clachair climbs the bare walls alone in the wind to judge whether the stone has shifted; it has not.

events.title: Uisdean mac Lachlainn named keeper of Taigh-solais Baile chrom
events.body: Uisdean mac Lachlainn of the headland villages is named the beacon's first keeper, on the recommendation of the very masons who built it: Dùghall Clachair among them, who signed the letter along with two of his crew.
